title: It's The End of the World and My TV Won't Turn Off
materials: Monitors, Dirt, 60 minutes of television footage, Television Remote
description: Made for the //PIXELMOUTH show “IT’S THE END OF THE WORLD AND MY EARS ARE BLEEDING AND MY EYES ARE BURNING AND MY MOUTH IS FALLING OUT” at LaMaMa gallery, this piece explores the tendency to numb reality through media overconsumption. Contextualized by a show theme of imminent apocalypse, this media piece is a collection of clips aired on television that each allude to apocalypse in their own way. From televangelist rants to buzzer beaters, reality TV show break ups to ACME explosions from cartoons, there is no escape from the inevitable no matter how many channels you surf through. Media clips were collated in Touchdesigner allowing for viewers to surf channels in real time through the use of a television remote.
imageAlt: It's The End of the World

title: Keeping Receipts
description: Sparked by a desire to reframe screen time and give physical form to media overconsumption, Keeping Receipts is a sculptural piece that physically documents every social media post a viewer scrolls by in real time. By converting intangible digital excess into an accumulating stream of thermal paper, the work exposes the volume, velocity, and banality of the content we ingest without noticing. What is usually invisible becomes permanently material, inviting the viewer to confront the impacts of their own attention economy.

title: The New York Name Change Game
description: Inspired by MSCHF’s Tax Heaven 3000, this website is an interactive, text based game that guides a player narratively through the New York name change petition form. Grounded in community research, this project aims to solve the pain point that many queer individuals face of the daunting process that is legally changing your name. Through enacting play, I aim to make this process more approachable by turning it into an interactive, 15 minute guided experience. The game asks for required information throughout its runtime, storing the answers locally in a user’s browser before returning a filled PDF document ready to be printed and submitted at a courthouse to begin a petition.
imageAlt: The New York Name Change Game

title: Chopom
materials: Metal, Arduino, Microphone, Receipt Printer, ChatGPT API
description: At the start of 2025 my grandmother passed away. In my grief two parts of that experience stood out to me. The first was that my grandmother, while bedridden, always had her dog by her side. The second was when I walked past my father’s office a few weeks after she had passed and saw ChatGPT open with a conversation about how to handle grief. These experiences made me think about the different forms of guidance and comfort we seek during periods of uncertainty, eventually leading me to researching the mythological concept of the psychopomp, a guide and escort from the living world to the afterlife that appears throughout cultures. This interactive sculpture is a recontextualization of large language models as a mythological psychopomp. Viewers are invited to speak about their doubts and struggles to the metal sculpture of a dog’s mouth and are met with advice generated by a large language model printed on a receipt. This project questions what ways technology will come to comfort us in the future, and in what ways will it always fall short of that goal?

title: TouchDesigner Works
description: A collection of works created in TouchDesigner, a visual programming language for creating real time visual systems. Explorations of entropy, algorithims, and audio-reactive systems inspire me while keeping my scripting skills sharp!
